cefrAlignment: B1-appropriate (CEFR CV identifying cues and inferring: can extrapolate the meaning of occasional unknown words from the context on familiar topics): the passages are about 220 words with a few glossed B1/B2 target words, and the tasks practise definition, example, contrast and word-part clues.
examFidelity: Closest-in-meaning items reflect TOEFL Read an Academic Passage vocabulary questions and TOEIC Part 7 synonym questions; I removed the unverified 'highlighted word' format detail and softened the claim that IELTS questions 'almost always' paraphrase.
fixes: Added 'ir-' (irregular) to the word-parts list, because ex2 tests 'irreparable' as a word-parts clue and that prefix was never taught
Corrected the 'thrive' walkthrough: the example clues come both before and after the word, not only 'after it'
Improved the 'unstable' grammar reasoning (it describes the bridge, rather than 'it comes after was, so it is an adjective')
Hedged the phone-checking claim in the practice passage ('Some surveys suggest…')
TOEFL tip: replaced 'a highlighted word' with 'a word in the passage' (unverified format detail); IELTS tip: 'almost always' → 'often'
Replaced an unnatural vocabulary example ('Is Monday morning inconvenient for you?')
learnerOutcome: A learner can decide whether an unknown word matters and, when it does, work out an approximate meaning from definition, example, contrast and nearby-explanation clues and from common prefixes and suffixes.
